content.thinking:
I'm putting together the postmortem and noting the key facts: the monthly-spend feature flag was switched on by an admin at P1, and ZeroDivisionError errors hit spend_summary.py line 47 between 03:30 and 03:39. Before that, with the flag off, the pages rendered normally.

I'm checking the flag logs for the window after Argus's revert: the monthly-spend flag still shows "on" evaluations from 03:37 to 03:39, and the errors kept coming. That suggests the flag-off change never reached the service, so I'll note that as the reason the revert didn't help. The next step to stop the harm is to switch the flag off again and confirm the service logs "off" evaluations and the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 stops.

I'm checking whether the root cause is actually established: the log shows the ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47, but not yet that the divisor is this month's purchase count for shoppers with none. I'm also weighing whether the mechanism rests on a row in the data that doesn't show it.

I'm now working out the causal chain for the postmortem: shoppers' account pages failed, traced to a ZeroDivisionError at spend_summary.py:47 during the 03:30 window. I still need to pin down why those requests hit that line, which means tying the flag switch-on at P1 to the monthly spend summary path.

I'm checking whether any deploy shows up in the change events, and the reads so far only turn up flag toggles, so no deploy is in play. The pages were healthy with the flag off, so the flag switch is the change that lines up with the onset. Background client-disconnect errors appear before 03:30 as well, which looks like ordinary noise rather than the cause.

I'm working out how the flag reaches the code: the flag routes account pages through average_spend_per_item_this_month, which divides by this month's purchase count, and that count is zero for shoppers with no purchases yet this month.

I'm writing up the contributing factors now, starting with the missing test: nothing exercised the monthly spend path for accounts with no purchases this month before the flag went on in production. The fix I'm weighing is requiring tests on the flag-on path before a flag is enabled.

I'm noting two more contributing factors: the flag was switched fully on at once, going from 8 of 200 requests to all 200 within a minute, with no staged rollout or error-based halt in view. And the broad handler in serve_account_page turns any exception into a failed page, so the whole page fails instead of just the spend summary.

I'm also weighing a missing alert: nobody was paged, since the alert routing for the high error rate doesn't page on-call, so I'll propose routing it there. And the revert appears not to have reached the service, with "on" evaluations still logged from 03:37 to 03:39, which I'll cover under why the mitigation failed rather than as a contributing factor.

I'm checking the earlier incident 9c1d4e7a, which I found in memory, where someone also tried reverting monthly-spend-feature and it was judged refuted, so this same flag revert has failed before.

Checking the wrap-up sections now: one earlier incident in memory reached the same flag revert and got it refuted, yet I tried that revert again without first asking why it hadn't worked back then. The got-lucky section has nothing I can support, so I'll leave it empty, and the went-well list is still blank.

I'm now going through the postmortem sections: the investigator's start at the onset, the candidate cause that named the flag and failing line, the Mitigation Agent putting the flag back on when the revert didn't help, and Code-Fix's draft PR. Next I'm drafting the prevention action items, starting with requiring tests on a feature flag's on path before it can be enabled in production.

I'm weighing how to phrase the prevention items: staging flag changes to io-shop with an automatic halt when the error rate rises, making the account page fall back to a page without the spend summary when that summary fails, and routing the high error rate alert to page on-call.

I'm drafting the remaining postmortem fields: a command to switch the flag off again and confirm the error line stops appearing in the logs, and a question for why the service kept logging the flag as on after the revert, which I'll check against whether the change reached the flag client at all.

I'm drafting the root-cause fields now, and the plain-words version needs to say that switching on the new monthly spending feature sent account pages through a calculation dividing by zero, probably for shoppers with no purchases yet this month, so the page failed instead of rendering.

I'm settling the root-cause wording: with the flag on, the spend summary's average divides this month's spend by this month's purchase count, which is zero for shoppers who bought before but not this month, so the ZeroDivisionError at line 47 fails the account page request.

I'm drafting the step-by-step timeline now, and for the first step I'm noting that account page requests failed with server errors from the onset while error rates ran far above normal. For the second step, the failures trace to a ZeroDivisionError raised when rendering those pages in the spend summary module, logged throughout the window.

I'm tying the onset to the flag: monthly-spend-feature was switched on by an admin, and the flag went from off to on across the service's evaluations within the same minute the division errors began. Deploys and client disconnects don't line up with that, since the pages rendered normally with the flag off.

I'm checking the Mitigation Agent's revert judgment against the flag logs, which still show monthly-spend-feature evaluating as on through 03:37 to 03:39, so the revert may never have reached the service.

I'm reviewing the went-well and went-wrong lists: the revert was judged refuted even though io-shop's flag evaluations still logged monthly-spend-feature as on through 03:37 to 03:39, and Argus repeated a revert that an earlier incident had already found refuted. The second investigation only retried the same flag change, so it added nothing new, while the Mitigation Agent's quick revert of the flag the errors started with is worth recording as a success.

action_items.item: Require that the code path a feature flag turns on in io-shop is covered by tests before that flag can be switched on in production.
Roll out io-shop feature flag changes to a small share of traffic first, then widen in stages.
Halt a staged flag rollout automatically, and switch the flag back, when the service's error rate rises above its baseline.
Make serve_account_page render the account page without the spend summary when the summary fails, instead of failing the whole page.
Route the HighErrorRate alert on io-shop to page the on-call person.

causal_chain.step: Shoppers' account page requests failed, and the service logged account page error rates far above their usual level.
The account page requests failed because building the page raised ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. The service logged this error throughout {G5309.3} and not before.

ruled_out.what: A deployment: the change events read held no deploys, only changes to the monthly-spend-feature flag.
Shoppers closing their connections, the account page error logged before the onset: it was logged only in {G46bc.3}, while account pages were rendering normally.

causal_chain.step: Requests reached that code because admin switched feature flag monthly-spend-feature on at {P1.1}. The service evaluated the flag as off up to {G7e5d.4}, partly on in {G971b.6}, and on for every evaluation from {Gce95.4}. The division errors began in that same minute.

Switching the flag on broke the page because, as Code-Fix read the source, the flag sends account pages through a monthly average per item whose divisor is zero for shoppers who have bought nothing yet this month.

input.cause_in_plain_words: Someone switched on a new monthly spending feature, and it sent shoppers' account pages through a calculation that divides by zero, likely for shoppers who had not bought anything yet this month, so those pages failed to load.

contributing_factors.factor: No test or check was seen that ran the code path monthly-spend-feature turns on against an account with no purchases this month before the flag was switched on in production. Code-Fix's reading says the existing tests do not cover that case.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: The division by zero would have been caught before the flag reached production shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-1

contributing_factors.factor: The flag went from a few evaluations on to every evaluation on in the next minute. No staged rollout and no automatic halt on rising errors were seen.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Only a small share of account page requests would have failed, and the rollout could have stopped before it reached all shoppers.
contributing_factors.label: CF-2

contributing_factors.factor: As Code-Fix read the source, a broad handler in serve_account_page turns any exception in the spend summary into a failed account page rather than leaving that section out.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: Shoppers would still have got their account page, just without the spend summary, even with the division by zero still in place.
contributing_factors.label: CF-3

contributing_factors.factor: No on-call person was paged when the HighErrorRate alert fired on io-shop.
contributing_factors.had_it_been_otherwise: A person would have known of the failing pages and could have stepped in when the automated revert did not end the errors, which may have shortened the incident.
contributing_factors.label: CF-4

went_well.item: The Investigator Agent placed the start of the incident at the onset.
The Investigator Agent named the monthly-spend-feature flag change and the failing division in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py as the leading candidate.
The Mitigation Agent reverted monthly-spend-feature, the change the errors began with.
The Mitigation Agent switched monthly-spend-feature back on when the revert was judged not to help, so the service was left as Argus had found it.
The Code-Fix Agent proposed a fix as draft pull request #548.

went_wrong: The Mitigation Agent judged the revert refuted while io-shop's own flag evaluations still logged monthly-spend-feature=on in {Gce95.5}, after the flag had been switched off.

Argus found an earlier incident in memory, 9c1d4e7a-0000-4000-8000-00000000fee1, where reverting this same flag had been refuted, and tried the same revert again without first finding out why it had not helped then.
The second investigation formed only C2, which blamed the same flag change that had already been tried, so it gave Argus nothing new to try.

input.root_cause: With monthly-spend-feature on, render_spend_summary calls average_spend_per_item_this_month in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py. That function divides the account's spend this month by the number of purchases it made this month. The divisor is zero for any shopper who has bought before but not yet this month, so the account page request raises ZeroDivisionError.
input.still_at_risk: Account page requests could keep failing with a division by zero for as long as monthly-spend-feature stays on.
input.stops_the_harm: Switch monthly-spend-feature off again in a way that reaches io-shop. Confirm at the service that its flag evaluation log lines read monthly-spend-feature=off and that ZeroDivisionError in src/io_shop/spend_summary.py is no longer logged for account page requests.
input.why_it_did_not_help: Find out why io-shop kept logging monthly-spend-feature=on evaluations after the flag was switched off at {P2.1}: whether the change reached the service's flag evaluation at all, and if so through what cache or refresh. If it did reach the service, find out why account pages still failed.
